name: Red-headed Quelea
rangeDescription: Grassland of sub-saharan africa
description: The red head of the breeding male is distinctive. Non-breeding male and female are nondescript, streaky brown birds with buffy eyebrows.

name: Great Thick-knee
rangeDescription: Southeastern iran to indian subcontinent, indochina, and hainan
description: An odd-looking wader with a dark mask, staring pale eyes, and a large heavy bill. Flashing black-and-white wingtips, revealed in flight, recall those of lapwings.

name: Cuban Martin
rangeDescription: Cuba including isla de la juventud (isle of pines; south of western cuba)
description: A graceful aerial feeder found over a wide variety of open habitats, especially near water, including marshes and towns. Often chooses exposed perches including power and telephone lines in villages.

name: Blyth's Pipit
rangeDescription: Southern siberia to mongolia, china, tibet, and northeastern india
description: A mid-sized pipit with pale brown plumage and a fine, dark bill. Strong streaking on the head, mantle, and back contrasts strongly with the pale edges of the feathers.

name: Malayan Crested Fireback
rangeDescription: Thai-malay peninsula and sumatra
description: Flamboyant dark pheasant of tropical lowland rainforest, typically in wetter areas. Male is glossy blue-black with a tufted crest, electric blue facial skin, blood-red back and white tail.

name: Daurian Starling
rangeDescription: Southeastern siberia to northern mongolia and northern korea; winters to southeastern asia
description: Small, strongly migratory starling; common on its wintering grounds, but localized when breeding, and often difficult to find when on migration. Male dark above, white below, but intricately patterned, with shades of violet, green, and orange in wings.

name: African Fish-Eagle
rangeDescription: Sub-saharan africa
description: The adult is a large, distinctive, chestnut-and-white eagle that sits prominently on perches near rivers, lakes, and other waterbodies. The scruffy immature is dark brown and mottled with white on head.

name: Philippine Collared-Dove
rangeDescription: Philippines and sulu archipelago; vagrant to northern borneo; introduced to northern marianas (guam north to saipan)
description: Brownish dove with a short collar of large dark scales, a gray head, and a pinkish flush on the neck and breast. Native to the Philippines, where now declining and uncommon; fairly common in introduced range (Guam and Northern Mariana Islands).

name: Smew
rangeDescription: Northern eurasia; winters to north africa, india, and eastern china
description: Generally uncommon and fairly local small diving duck. Frequents lakes, reservoirs, and rivers.

name: Black-and-buff Woodpecker
rangeDescription: Humid forest of myanmar, thailand, and indochina
description: Adorably tiny and stout woodpecker. Triangular crest makes the head seem disproportionately large at a distance.
imageCreditName: Lars Petersson | My World of Bird Photography

name: Red-necked Buzzard
rangeDescription: Sub-saharan and west-central africa; disperses to sahel
description: This is the common buzzard of much of the Sahel in north, west, and central Africa. Typically has a brown back, a dark chest, a black-spotted white belly, and a rufous tail.

name: Rufous-winged Antshrike
rangeDescription: Lowlands of northeastern bolivia to northeastern paraguay and eastern and central brazil
description: Medium-sized antshrike. Males have black-and-white barring on the breast and tail and a black crown that fades to gray on the back.

name: McConnell's Spinetail
rangeDescription: Tepuis of southern venezuela, adjacent brazil, guyana, and suriname
description: Dark, long-tailed, sparrow-sized bird of dense thickets. Body plumage is mostly dark gray with a bright rufous cap and wings.

name: Whyte's Francolin
rangeDescription: Southeastern democratic republic of the congo to northern zambia and northern malawi
description: Medium-sized, cryptically-patterned francolin. Shows rufous patches in the wings in flight.

name: Peruvian Antpitta
rangeDescription: East slope of andes of southeastern ecuador and far northern peru
description: Small, very rare antpitta of Andean cloud forest understory. Despite its name, most sightings are from the east slope of the Andes in Ecuador.

name: Heard Island Shag
rangeDescription: Heard island (southern indian ocean)
description: Learn about Imperial Cormorant (Heard Island): explore photos, sounds, and observations collected by birders around the world.

name: Black-backed Oriole
rangeDescription: Riparian woodland of central plateau and eastern mexico
description: Attractive orange-and-black oriole endemic to central Mexico, where it takes the place of Bullock’s Oriole (of western North America). Favors open woods, plantations, hedges with tall trees, and towns; migrants also occur in pine-oak forest in mountains.

name: Persian Wheatear
rangeDescription: Breeds from northeastern türkiye, southern armenia, azerbaijan, and iran eastward to southern turkmenistan, southern tajikistan (pamir range), afghanistan, and far northwestern pakistan; winters from the southern arabian peninsula and southern iraq eastward to pakistan and northwestern india
description: A medium-sized wheatear, gray-brown overall with a reddish tail base. Sexes similar.

name: Dusky-backed Jacamar
rangeDescription: Tropical eastern panama and northwestern colombia
description: Distinctive within limited range near the border of Panama and Colombia. Typical jacamar shape with extremely long, pointed bill and an upright stance.

name: Sandy Gallito
rangeDescription: Andean slope of argentina (southwestern salta to río negro)
description: Plain brown thrush-sized bird of the Monte desert region of western Argentina. Note shorter, thicker bill than canasteros, miners and thornbirds.
